messages:
maya: heads-up: after last night's allocator layout change we saw a collapse in prefix cache hit-rate on conv-chat routes
jon: yep alerts just hit my inbox — p99 jumped ~30ms and cache_hit_rate fell from ~0.74 to ~0.18 :grimacing:
perf-bot: [ALERT] route=/v1/chat model=redwood-conv-3b p99=112ms (baseline=80ms) | prefix_cache_hit_rate=0.18 (baseline=0.74)
maya: digging into the sampler logs on shard-4. Keys generated for apparently identical requests are different. looks like trailing bytes differ
priya: can you paste the key function we use currently? want to see normalization pipeline
maya: simplified runtime key: `key = sha256(f"{model}|{prompt_bytes}|{session}|{seq}")`
kevin: the allocator change now trims unused capacity in some buffers, previously we carried trailing zeros. that will change raw prompt_bytes if we use underlying buffer slices
jon: i captured a few keys from canary vs prod for same request id — they diverge at the tail bytes, identical human tokens though
jon: sample hex diff: `canary: ...ff12 ab00 prod: ...ff12 ab`
priya: so one has explicit 0x00 padding, the other doesn't. since we hash the raw bytes that's a hard mismatch
maya: our canonicalize step only normalizes whitespace and unicode: `normalize(s) = s.strip().casefold()` — doesn't handle embedded NULs or capacity padding
kevin: long-term fix: derive key from token ids and token length (tokenizer provides exact length), not raw byte buffers. that's deterministic across allocators
priya: building keys from ids is safer but adds CPU to keying. we should benchmark the overhead (p50/p95 key latency)
maya: short-term mitigation: patch the normalizer to trim trailing NULs and compress internal NUL runs to a canonical marker so padding doesn't change hash
jon: quick local fuzz shows current hashes differ with small pads: script: `for pad in [0,1,4,8]: s = orig + b"\x00"*pad; print(pad, sha256(normalize(s)).hexdigest())` -> different outputs
priya: ok please add unit tests covering padded buffers + different tokenizer backends (py vs c++)
staging-bot: rollback recommended for allocator-layout on shard-4 due to cache-hit regression
deploy-bot: rollback executed at 02:41 UTC by @deploy-bot
maya: after rollback hit-rate climbed back to ~0.71 within ~4 minutes, p99 returned to baseline
kevin: action items: 1) short patch to normalizer (trim trailing NULs) 2) longer fix: switch key derivation to token-id based (ENG-8531) 3) add CI smoke that randomizes allocator padding
jon: i'll open a tiny runtime PR with normalizer change + tests (including fuzz pads and a C++ tokenizer binary fixture)
priya: i'll run microbenchmarks on key derivation CPU cost. if token-id approach adds >2us median we need to hide cost by coalescing with request parsing
maya: also add an e2e canary with allocator layout + normalizer patch before enabling layout cluster-wide
kevin: note for ops: we should have an alert that correlates sudden cache-hit drop with recent deploys to allocator or tokenizer libs
maya: ticket created ENG-8531 with graphs, hex diffs, and a perf runbook. linking perf traces and sample requests
perf-bot: [INFO] after PR lands, re-profile key derivation p50/p95 and verify hit-rate recovery on canary for 30m window
jon: ping me once PR merged, i'll coordinate canary test and include the pad-fuzz harness
maya: thanks team. learned lesson: canonicalization must be resilient to allocator/layout changes. we'll keep key derivation in token-space long term :partyparrot:
